survey: A gold five-pointed sheriff star badge floats against a purple sunburst, with no ground plane. The star is a slab with bevelled arms: a centre ridge runs down each arm and meets at the middle. Each of the five tips ends in a gold ball, which reads as a sphere from any angle. A red domed gem sits in a round gold bezel at the centre. The badge faces the viewer almost head-on with a slight turn. A thin rim of thickness shows along the lower-right edges, which suggests a view from slightly above and to the left. The arms are spaced roughly evenly (about 65–79° apart), but their lengths vary. The top and right arms are longest, and the lower-left arm is clearly shorter and stubbier. The gem bezel looks almost perfectly circular, which fits a face-on view. The tip balls sit naturally at the arm ends. No other parts or repeated surface elements need to follow a tilted plane.

errors.where: Star body versus centre gem bezel, especially the lower-left arm
errors.what: The arms have unequal lengths, and the lower-left arm is noticeably shorter. This reads as if the badge is tilted with its lower-left side turned away. But the centre bezel and gem are drawn as a near-perfect circle, as if seen straight on. Either the star is slightly lopsided, or the star and the bezel imply two slightly different viewing angles.

fix: A symmetrical sheriff star badge with five equal-length arms evenly spaced at 72 degrees, seen straight on with only a slight tilt. The round centre bezel and red gem are foreshortened by the same tilt as the star. All five ball tips sit at equal distance from the centre.
